sections.heading: Coming to the God who holds me up
sections.text: Blessed God, you are full of life and joy in yourself. You do not need anything from me, yet every true joy I have comes from you. You made me, you have been good to me, I belong to you, and you keep me alive even when I forget how dependent I am. You have carried me, provided for me, been patient with me, saved me, and kept me. Whatever situation I am in, and whatever weakness or trouble I bring to you, you are able to meet me there.
theological_themes: God is self-sufficient and blessed in himself.
God is Creator, owner, provider, and sustainer of his creatures.
The believer depends on God in every need and misery.

scripture_references.connection: Paul describes God as the Creator who is not served as though he needed anything, because he gives life and breath to all. This grounds the prayer’s confession that God is self-sufficient while I am completely dependent on him.
This psalm portrays God as the generous provider who satisfies the needs of his creatures. It supports the prayer’s trust that God can meet me in every circumstance.

sections.heading: Wanting to live from you and for you
sections.text: Let my life be rooted in you and aimed back toward you. Do not let me grow comfortable with a shallow or half-hearted faith. Keep me dissatisfied with any progress that does not make me more like Jesus. Shape my values, my reactions, my desires, and my ordinary choices so that his way of life becomes more and more visible in me.
theological_themes: The Christian life is lived by dependence on God and for God’s glory.
Growth in holiness means being conformed to Christ in character and conduct.
Believers should not be complacent about spiritual growth.

scripture_references.connection: Paul says God’s purpose for his people is that they be conformed to the image of his Son. This directly supports the prayer’s longing to resemble Christ rather than settle for outward religion.
Paul describes the Christian life as life in Christ, lived by faith in the Son of God. That gives biblical shape to asking to live by God and for God.

sections.heading: Letting your love make obedience a joy
sections.text: Father, let your unmatched love for me move me from the inside out. I do not want obedience to feel like a cold transaction or a way to earn your approval. Let your mercy make me willing, steady, and glad to do what pleases you. Teach me to love your will, not merely submit to it.
theological_themes: God’s love is the motive and power for holy obedience.
Obedience is not a way to earn grace, but a grateful response to grace.
God can make duty become delight.

scripture_references.connection: Paul says the love of Christ controls believers so that they no longer live for themselves but for him. This grounds the prayer’s request that divine love would constrain the heart into glad obedience.
Jesus connects love for him with keeping his commandments. The prayer asks that obedience flow from love rather than bare obligation.

sections.heading: Being faithful when people misunderstand me
sections.text: If people think my trust in you is foolish, or my gentleness is weakness, or my zeal is too much, or my hope is make-believe, or my obedience is only for show, keep me from bitterness and self-pity. If I suffer because I belong to you, help me receive that with joy—not because pain is easy, but because your name is worth more than my reputation.
theological_themes: Faithfulness to God may be mocked or misunderstood by others.
Suffering for Christ’s name can be received with joy because belonging to him is greater than human approval.
The believer asks for humility and endurance under reproach.

scripture_references.connection: Jesus teaches his disciples to rejoice when they are reviled and falsely accused on his account. This supports the prayer’s desire to endure misunderstanding for God’s name with joy.
Peter encourages Christians not to be ashamed when they suffer as Christians, but to glorify God in that name. This fits the prayer’s request to remain faithful when obedience is misread or despised.

sections.heading: Keeping my eyes on my true home
sections.text: Keep me walking steadily toward the home you have promised, the everlasting joy that is my real inheritance. Strengthen me with help from heaven so I do not turn back. Guard my heart from chasing pleasures that look bright for a moment but fade into nothing. By your grace, keep me moving toward what will last forever.
theological_themes: The believer is a pilgrim whose true inheritance is with God.
Perseverance depends on God’s sustaining strength.
Temporary sinful pleasures cannot compare with the lasting joy God promises.

scripture_references.connection: Hebrews describes believers as strangers and exiles seeking a better, heavenly country. This supports the prayer’s picture of life as a journey toward the believer’s true inheritance.
Peter speaks of an imperishable inheritance kept by God and believers being guarded by God’s power. This grounds the prayer’s confidence that God can keep me moving toward eternal joy.
The call to run with endurance while looking to Jesus fits the prayer’s plea not to turn back or be distracted by what cannot last.

sections.heading: Giving me one clear purpose
sections.text: As you carry me on this journey, make my life simple in the best way. Let people see that I am not living for a dozen competing ambitions. Give me a burning desire for you, and make me genuinely useful for the good and salvation of other people. Let love for you and love for my neighbor become the clear direction of my life.
theological_themes: Love for God is the believer’s highest aim.
Love for others includes concern for their good and salvation.
A life of discipleship should become focused, wholehearted, and useful to God.

scripture_references.connection: Jesus identifies love for God and love for neighbor as the great commandments on which the Law and Prophets depend. This gives biblical grounding to the prayer’s request for one clear aim: desire for God and the good of others.

Paul describes becoming all things to all people so that some might be saved, doing it for the sake of the gospel. This supports the prayer’s concern not only for personal holiness but also for the salvation of others.

content_provenance.original_author: Unattributed Puritan source (compiled and edited by Arthur Bennett)
content_provenance.original_source: The Valley of Vision: A Collection of Puritan Prayers and Devotions, ed. Arthur Bennett (The Banner of Truth Trust)
content_provenance.source_copyright_status: Compilation, titles and arrangement in copyright (Banner of Truth, 1975); underlying Puritan sources are public domain.
content_provenance.modern_version_note: Contemporary prayer based on the theological themes and ideas of the historical source; not a reproduction of the original wording.

theological_issues_identified: The phrase 'happy in thyself' reflects the classical doctrine of God’s blessedness and self-sufficiency. I rendered it as God being full of life and joy in himself, avoiding any implication that God’s happiness fluctuates like human emotion.

The original’s language about false pleasures 'that wilt and disappear into nothing' could refer broadly to worldly or sinful delights. I kept that concrete contrast without implying that all earthly enjoyment is wrong.
significant_interpretive_choices: 'Proprietor' was rendered as 'I belong to you' to preserve the idea of God’s rightful ownership while keeping the prayer personal and natural.

'Conformity to his principles, temper, and conduct' was interpreted as Christlikeness in values, reactions, desires, and ordinary choices, because the original is concerned with both inner disposition and outward behavior.

'The good and salvation of my fellow men' was rendered as concern for the good and salvation of other people, preserving both practical love and evangelistic concern without retaining gendered language.
